clue.text: Tips for raising the bridge

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading the bridge word from bottom to top

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one

explanation.surface: Advice on how a drawbridge is hoisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns SPAN upwards in this down entry, giving NAPS. 'Tips' is a racing word: a nap is a tipster's strongest selection.
explanation.definitionFit: In British horse racing a nap is a tipster's most confident pick, so tips can be called naps.

clue.text: Girl in army dress

indicators.note: to dress troops is to arrange them in line, so the letters of army are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A young woman wearing military uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like clothing but is the anagram signal, in the parade-ground sense of lining up soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Myra is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Hearing viewed as painful

indicators.note: on hearing, the word for viewed is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: viewed means saw

explanation.surface: Someone's hearing is judged to be painful.
explanation.walkthrough: In standard British speech, with no sounded R, the past tense of see and the word for aching are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sore hurts, the same as painful or aching.

clue.text: Palindrome dropped and rewritten with appeal

indicators.note: the letters left over are written again in a new order
the letters of the word and are let fall from Palindrome, one by one

explanation.surface: A palindrome was abandoned and redrafted with more charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes A, N, D out of PALINDROME, leaving PLIROME; 'rewritten' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to beg earnestly, which is to appeal to someone.

clue.text: Used to be found on watch?

explanation.surface: Something that was once used is now kept on guard duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on watch' suggests a sentry, but it is a wristwatch, whose fastest-moving pointer counts the seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Used goods are pre-owned; a timepiece's thin hand ticking off each sixty seconds is the other sense.

clue.text: A small marsupial, one born after the war

explanation.surface: A little pouched animal turns out to be a postwar child.
explanation.walkthrough: A boomer is a large male kangaroo, so the pun reads a young one as a baby of that kind; the phrase also names someone born in the birth surge after 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-1945 births rose sharply, so that generation took the boom label; a joey kangaroo is the whimsical second reading.

clue.text: Notices lists of names

explanation.surface: Official notices posted as rolls of names.
explanation.definitionFit: To register something is to notice it, and a register is an official roll or record of names.

clue.text: Complaint from second class — charge for return

parts.note: B is the label for second class or grade

indicators.note: for return asks for the charge word to be sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: a charge is a fee

explanation.surface: A grumble from someone in second class about a refund of the fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for return' sounds like a return ticket, but it reverses FEE to EEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal slang for a grievance or grumble.

clue.text: "Spreading out" means "born to farming in America"

parts.note: ranching is livestock farming as practised in the United States

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style entry claiming a word's meaning comes from a farming birth in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree branching divides into limbs, so it is extending outwards in several directions.

clue.text: Get going when fish shelter in stormy gales

indicators.note: the fish takes shelter inside the rearranged letters of gales
stormy shows the letters of gales thrown into disorder

parts.note: the hake is a common food fish

explanation.surface: Time to move when fish hide from a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' rearranges the letters of gales to SALEG, and the fish shelters inside it right after the S; 'shake a leg' is an idiom for hurrying.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hurry up and start moving, the same as get going.

clue.text: Weekend like this, back on a holiday island

parts.note: the end of the word week is its last letter, K

indicators.note: back means the word for like this is written in reverse

parts.note: so means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A weekend spent this way, returning to a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weekend' reads as Saturday and Sunday, but it means the final letter of week. 'back' turns SO into OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Kos is a Greek island in the Dodecanese, a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Swear on the bible? No point

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
no, as in nil, is the round letter O
W is west, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Asked to swear on the Bible, someone sees no point.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a courtroom oath; in fact the Bible gives AV, 'No' is O for nought, and 'point' is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare solemnly, as one does when swearing an oath.

clue.text: One working with a particle

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
on means working or switched on, as a machine is

explanation.surface: A labourer partnered with a tiny particle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ion is an electrically charged atom or molecule, a kind of particle in physics.

clue.text: Transitive nouns

parts.note: transitive is read as words that let you transit, that is, words which let a person go through a checkpoint

explanation.walkthrough: 'Transitive' looks like grammar for a verb with an object, which makes 'nouns' feel contradictory; it means words for getting through.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret word giving entry lets its holder pass a guard or a login, so it is a word for transit.

clue.text: Ezra makes his mark, and sees the possibility of money

explanation.surface: A poet autographs his work and spots a chance of profit.
explanation.walkthrough: Ezra Pound was an American poet, so the poet writing his name is Pound signing; a cartoon character dreaming of profit has £ symbols in their eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The £ symbol is Britain's currency mark; the poet's surname plus his autographing gives the other reading.

clue.text: Chamber that helps cure for a change

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of helps cure are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A room that aids a remedy, just to be different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' sounds like a casual aside, but it rearranges the nine letters of HELPS CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepulchre is a tomb, a burial room cut in rock or built of stone.

clue.text: Bread used for catching fish?

parts.note: white is the common type of sliced bread
bait is what is used to catch fish or animals

explanation.surface: Bread used by an angler to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as an angler's tip; the question mark admits that the tiny fish is not literally caught with bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitebait are the small young of herring and sprat, eaten whole as a fried fish dish.

clue.text: The secret language of fish — English!

parts.note: the cod is a large sea fish

explanation.surface: Fish secretly communicate in English.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a system of symbols for hiding meaning, a secret way of communicating.

clue.text: Ask the family for fruit

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them persistently
kin are one's relatives or family

explanation.surface: Request some fruit from relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the large orange gourd is a fruit, a seed-bearing body of the plant.

clue.text: What is the point of medical treatment?

indicators.note: treatment shows the letters of medical being worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks what good medical treatment does.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a doubting question; 'the point of' is the dot in a number written with tenths and hundredths.
explanation.definitionFit: The dot separating whole units from fractions is called the decimal point, so that number system owns the point.

clue.text: Finished with game point to exceed the limit

parts.note: over means finished or ended
RU is Rugby Union, a ball game
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: With the match ending on a winning point, play runs on too long.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go beyond a set time or boundary, which is going past the limit.

clue.text: Hero's response at wedding to first love

parts.note: I do is the vow said by bride and groom at a wedding

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of love

explanation.surface: A hero's reply at the altar to his first sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero's' is read as hero is, with the 's as a link meaning the word for hero is what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone admired and worshipped, much like a hero.

clue.text: Give a send off that could be foreseen

indicators.note: off says the letters of give a send are knocked out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A farewell party that might have been predicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a send off' reads as a farewell, but 'off' is the anagram signal on GIVE A SEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage something is to picture it in advance, which is to foresee it.

clue.text: Behave with discretion when topless

indicators.note: topless means the top, or first letter in a down entry, is removed

parts.note: tact is discretion or diplomacy

explanation.surface: Advice to act discreetly when not wearing a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' suggests nudity but removes the first letter of TACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to conduct oneself, which is behaving in a particular way.

clue.text: Horse chestnut or beech first of all

indicators.note: first of all takes the opening letter of every one of the words before it

explanation.surface: Choosing between a chestnut horse and a beech tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse chestnut' looks like a tree name, but 'Horse' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cob is a sturdy short-legged breed of horse.

clue.text: Almost dark, but not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word for dark is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day

explanation.surface: It is nearly dark outside, though not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims the final T from NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh means near, so to be nigh on something is to be almost there.

clue.text: Skywriting?

parts.note: skywriting is read not as smoke words traced by a plane but as a written message sent by air

explanation.walkthrough: An aerogramme was a lightweight sheet folded into its own envelope for cheap airmail.
explanation.definitionFit: A single folded sheet sent by airmail is correspondence carried through the sky.

clue.text: A type of chamber in an east Caribbean house

parts.note: C is short for Caribbean

explanation.surface: A special kind of room in an East Caribbean home.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverberating room used for recording effects is called an echo chamber.

clue.text: Fish barrel — heart of oak

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel or cask

indicators.note: heart of takes the central letter of oak

explanation.surface: Fish kept in an oak barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish, often tinned.

clue.text: Vogue was an overpowering passion

explanation.surface: A fashion that was a consuming obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all the rage is in fashion; the word also means violent anger.

clue.text: In the past I hung round college

indicators.note: the word for I hangs around the college letter, enclosing it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone recalls loitering around their old college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the Roman numeral, read as ONE, which goes round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some earlier time.

clue.text: Dangerous contact with energy

parts.note: touch is physical contact
and means together with
go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: Coming into contact with live energy is hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a risky, precarious situation whose outcome is uncertain.
